subject: general
question: As reported in May 2025, which of the following banks of India provided in-principle approval to PayPal and Worldline to operate as cross-border payment aggregators in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Reserve Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, as the primary regulator of the Indian financial system, granted in-principle approval to global payment leaders **PayPal** and **Worldline** to operate as **Cross-Border Payment Aggregators (PA-CB)** in **May 2025**.
 
• This approval allows these entities to facilitate **cross-border transactions** for **import** and **export** of goods and services, bringing them under the direct regulatory purview of the **central bank**.
 
• The **PA-CB** license is a specialized category introduced by the **RBI** to regulate intermediaries that handle online international payments, ensuring better transparency and security in **foreign exchange** flows. ***Hence, the correct answer is Reserve Bank of India.***
 
• By obtaining this in-principle approval, **PayPal** and **Worldline** can now move toward full authorization, provided they meet the compliance and **net worth** criteria specified by the **RBI**.
 
• The move is part of the **RBI's** broader framework, originally released in October 2023</str
